claim: The TORC1 regulator GATOR1/SEACIT controls meiotic entry and early meiotic events in yeast.
source: The TORC1 regulator GATOR1/SEACIT controls meiotic entry and early meiotic events in yeast.
evidence: This statement is presented in the abstract as established knowledge about yeast systems.

claim: In mutants of the GATOR2 component mio, meiotic DSBs trigger the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity.
source: We find that in mutants of the GATOR2 component mio, meiotic DSBs trigger the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity and a permanent arrest in oocyte growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including Western blots and immunofluorescence.

claim: In mutants of the GATOR2 component mio, meiotic DSBs trigger a permanent arrest in oocyte growth.
source: We find that in mutants of the GATOR2 component mio, meiotic DSBs trigger the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity and a permanent arrest in oocyte growth.
evidence: This is supported by ovary size measurements and imaging data shown in the figures.

claim: In GATOR1 mutants, high TORC1 activity results in the delayed repair of meiotic DSBs.
source: Conversely, in GATOR1 mutants, high TORC1 activity results in the delayed repair of meiotic DSBs and the hyperactivation of p53.
evidence: This is supported by γ-H2Av foci quantification data presented in Figure 3.

claim: In GATOR1 mutants, high TORC1 activity results in the hyperactivation of p53.
source: Conversely, in GATOR1 mutants, high TORC1 activity results in the delayed repair of meiotic DSBs and the hyperactivation of p53.
evidence: This is supported by p53-GFP reporter data shown in Figure 5.

claim: GATOR1 inhibits retrotransposon expression in the presence of meiotic DSBs in a pathway that functions in parallel to p53.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that GATOR1 inhibits retrotransposon expression in the presence of meiotic DSBs in a pathway that functions in parallel to p53.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data and epistasis analysis with p53 mutants shown in Figure 8.

claim: TORC1 is a multi-protein complex that functions as a master regulator of metabolism.
source: Target of Rapamycin Complex 1 (TORC1) is a multi-protein complex that functions as a master regulator of metabolism (Loewith and Hall, 2011; Laplante and Sabatini, 2012a; Jewell and Guan, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: In the presence of adequate nutrients and positive upstream growth signals, TORC1 becomes active and functions to stimulate growth and inhibit catabolic metabolism through the phosphorylation of down-stream effector proteins.
source: In the presence of adequate nutrients and positive upstream growth signals, TORC1, which contains the serine/threonine kinase Target of Rapamycin, becomes active and functions to stimulate growth and inhibit catabolic metabolism through the phosphorylation of down-stream effector proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TORC1 function.

claim: SEACIT/GATOR1 inhibits TORC1 activity in response to amino acid limitation.
source: The Seh1 Associated Complex Inhibits TORC1 (SEACIT), originally identified in yeast, inhibits TORC1 activity in response to amino acid limitation (Neklesa and Davis, 2009; Dokudovskaya et al., 2011; Wu and Tu, 2011; Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Panchaud et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: SEACIT/GATOR1 is comprised of three highly conserved proteins Npr2/Nprl2, Npr3/Nprl3 and Iml1/Depdc5.
source: SEACIT, known as the GAP Activity Towards Rags complex 1 (GATOR1) in metazoans, is comprised of three highly conserved proteins Npr2/Nprl2, Npr3/Nprl3 and Iml1/Depdc5 (Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Panchaud et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In Drosophila and mammals, depleting any of the three GATOR1 components results in increased TORC1 activity and growth.
source: In Drosophila and mammals, depleting any of the three GATOR1 components results in increased TORC1 activity and growth, as well as a reduced response to amino acid starvation (Kowalczyk et al., 2012; Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2014; Dutchak et al., 2015; Cai et al., 2016; Marsan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: In Drosophila and mammals, depleting any of the three GATOR1 components results in a reduced response to amino acid starvation.
source: In Drosophila and mammals, depleting any of the three GATOR1 components results in increased TORC1 activity and growth, as well as a reduced response to amino acid starvation (Kowalczyk et al., 2012; Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2014; Dutchak et al., 2015; Cai et al., 2016; Marsan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The role of the SEACIT/GATOR1 complex in the regulation of TORC1 activity is highly conserved in eukaryotes.
source: Thus, the role of the SEACIT/GATOR1 complex in the regulation of TORC1 activity is highly conserved in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparative data across species mentioned in the preceding text.

claim: The GATOR2 complex inhibits the activity of GATOR1 and thus functions to activate TORC1.
source: The multi-protein GATOR2 complex, known as Seh1 Associated Complex Activates TORC1 (SEACAT) in yeast, inhibits the activity of GATOR1 and thus functions to activate TORC1 (Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2014) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: In metazoans, the GATOR2 complex functions in multiple amino acid sensing pathways.
source: In metazoans, the GATOR2 complex functions in multiple amino acid sensing pathways (Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Panchaud et al., 2013; Chantranupong et al., 2014; Parmigiani et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2015; Cai et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: In tissue culture cells, depleting GATOR2 components results in the constitutive activation of GATOR1 and the permanent downregulation of TORC1 activity.
source: In tissue culture cells, depleting GATOR2 components results in the constitutive activation of GATOR1 and the permanent downregulation of TORC1 activity (Bar-Peled et al., 2013; Wei and Lilly, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mutations in the GATOR2 component mio result in a block to oocyte growth and differentiation, due to the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity in the female germline.
source: For example, mutations in the GATOR2 component mio, result in a block to oocyte growth and differentiation, due to the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity in the female germline (Iida and Lilly, 2004; Wei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: mio is not required to maintain TORC1 activity in most somatic tissues of Drosophila.
source: However, mio is not required to maintain TORC1 activity in most somatic tissues of Drosophila (Wei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Blocking the formation of meiotic DSBs in the mio mutant background results in increased TORC1 activity.
source: We found that relative to ovaries from mio single mutants, mio, mei-W68 double mutants have increased levels of TORC1 activity as measured by the phosphorylation of S6K (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: mio2, mei-W681 mutants have TORC1 activity levels similar to that observed in mei-W681 single mutants.
source: Notably, mio2, mei-W681 mutants have TORC1 activity levels similar to that observed in mei-W681 single mutants (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Blocking the formation of meiotic DSBs partially rescues mio mutant fertility.
source: In addition to increasing TORC1 activity, blocking the formation of meiotic DSBs partially rescues mio mutant fertility, with mio2, mei-W681 double mutants laying approximately ten times more eggs than mio2 single mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by egg laying data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutants in the spnA homolog Rad51, which fail to repair meiotic DSBs, have decreased TORC1 activity relative to wild-type ovaries.
source: Finally, mutants in the spnA homolog Rad51, which fail to repair meiotic DSBs, also have decreased TORC1 activity relative to wild-type ovaries (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity in mio mutants is potentiated, at least in part, by the presence of meiotic DSBs.
source: From these data, we conclude that the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity in mio mutants is potentiated, at least in part, by the presence of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing rescue of TORC1 activity when DSBs are blocked.

claim: In Drosophila, oogenesis begins in region 1 of the germarium when a germline stem cell divides to produce a cystoblast that undergoes four mitotic divisions, with incomplete cytokinesis, to produce a 16 cell interconnected germline cyst.
source: In Drosophila, oogenesis begins in region 1 of the germarium when a germline stem cell divides to produce a cystoblast that undergoes four mitotic divisions, with incomplete cytokinesis, to produce a 16 cell interconnected germline cyst (Figure 2A) (de Cuevas et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila oogenesis, supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: In late region 2a of the germarium, Spo11/Mei-W68 generates the meiotic DSBs that initiate meiotic recombination.
source: In late region 2a of the germarium, Spo11/Mei-W68 generates the meiotic DSBs that initiate meiotic recombination (McKim and Hayashi-Hagihara, 1998; Hunter, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: By late region 2b, only a small fraction of oocytes retain unrepaired DSBs.
source: As meiosis proceeds, meiotic DSBs are repaired such that by late region 2b, only a small fraction of oocytes retain unrepaired DSBs (Mehrotra and McKim, 2006; Narbonne-Reveau and Lilly, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The levels of p4E-BP are low in the vast-majority of ovarian cysts undergoing mitotic divisions in region 1.
source: We found that the levels of p4E-BP are low in the vast-majority of ovarian cysts undergoing mitotic divisions in region 1 (Figure 2A',B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2.

claim: A small number (0.5 per germarium, n = 57) of region one ovarian cysts have dramatically higher levels of p4E-BP staining.
source: However, a small number (0.5 per germarium, n = 57) of region one ovarian cysts have dramatically higher levels of p4E-BP staining (Figure 2A", arrowhead).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and quantification.

claim: As ovarian cysts enter meiosis I in early region 2a of the germarium, the levels of p4E-BP are low.
source: As ovarian cysts enter meiosis I in early region 2a of the germarium, the levels of p4E-BP are low (Figure 2A',B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2.

claim: As ovarian cysts are encapsulated by follicle cells in germarial region 2b, the levels of p4E-BP begin to rise and remain above those observed in region one and early region 2a.
source: As ovarian cysts are encapsulated by follicle cells in germarial region 2b, the levels of p4E-BP begin to rise and remain above those observed in region one and early region 2a (Figure 2B, arrow).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In mio mutant ovarian cysts, p4E-BP levels remain low in germline cells in region 2b and beyond.
source: In contrast to what is observed in wild type, in mio mutant ovarian cysts, p4E-BP levels remain low in germline cells in region 2b and beyond (Figure 2C, arrow).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: mio, mei-w68 double mutant ovarian cysts have an approximately three-fold increase in p4E-BP staining in region 2b of the germarium relative to mio mutants.
source: Consistent with the western blot analysis, mio, mei-w68 double mutant ovarian cysts have an approximately three-fold increase in p4E-BP staining in region 2b of the germarium relative to mio mutants (Figure 2C,E and H)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and quantification shown in Figure 2.

claim: The increase in TORC1 activity in the mio, mei-w68 double mutants is restricted to the germline.
source: Notably, the increase in TORC1 activity in the mio, mei-w68 double mutants is restricted to the germline, consistent with blocking meiotic DSBs having cell autonomous effects on TORC1 activity in the germline.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunofluorescence data showing germline-specific effects.

claim: Ovarian cysts from spnA/Rad51 mutants, which do not repair meiotic DSBs, have reduced levels of p4E-BP staining.
source: Additionally, consistent with our western blot analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 2, ovarian cysts from spnA/Rad51 mutants, which do not repair meiotic DSBs, have reduced levels of p4E-BP staining (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: mio is required to oppose the downregulation of TORC1 activity triggered by the presence of meiotic DSBs.
source: Taken together these data strongly suggest that mio is required to oppose the downregulation of TORC1 activity triggered by the presence of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing rescue of TORC1 activity when DSBs are blocked in mio mutants.

claim: Removing chk2/loki activity in the mio mutant background partially rescued the mio mutant phenotype.
source: We determined that removing chk2/loki activity in the mio mutant background, by generating double-mutants of loki and mio null alleles, partially rescued the mio mutant phenotype (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by ovary size measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: mio2, loki6 double mutants are approximately twice the size of mio2 single mutants.
source: Specifically, we found that mio2, loki6 double mutants are approximately twice the size of mio2 single mutants.
evidence: This is supported by ovary size measurements.

claim: DSBs communicate to the TORC1 machinery at least in part through the checkpoint protein Chk2/Loki.
source: These data suggest that DSBs communicate to the TORC1 machinery at least in part through the checkpoint protein Chk2/Loki.
evidence: This is inferred from the genetic interaction data between loki and mio.

claim: The delay in meiotic entry observed in Drosophila GATOR1 mutants is not fully penetrant.
source: However, the delay in meiotic entry observed in Drosophila GATOR1 mutants is not fully penetrant and therefore unlikely to be the sole cause of the infertility observed in GATOR1 mutant females (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B) (Wei et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claim: During Drosophila oogenesis, the kinetics of DSB formation and repair can be followed using an antibody against the phosphorylated form of His2Av known as γ-His2Av.
source: During Drosophila oogenesis, the kinetics of DSB formation and repair can be followed using an antibody against the phosphorylated form of His2Av known as γ-His2Av (Madigan et al., 2002; Mehrotra and McKim, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Drosophila ovarian cysts generate meiotic DSBs after the initiation of synaptonemal complex (SC) formation in region 2a of the germarium.
source: Drosophila ovarian cysts generate meiotic DSBs after the initiation of synaptonemal complex (SC) formation in region 2a of the germarium (Carpenter, 1975; Jang et al., 2003; Mehrotra and McKim, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: γ-H2Av nuclear foci are first observed in the two pro-oocytes, which are in early pachytene.
source: γ-H2Av nuclear foci are first observed in the two pro-oocytes, which are in early pachytene (Jang et al., 2003; Mehrotra and McKim, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A small number of DSBs are also observed in the pro-nurse cells.
source: A small number of DSBs are also observed in the pro-nurse cells (Mehrotra and McKim, 2006; Narbonne-Reveau and Lilly, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: As meiosis proceeds and the DSBs are repaired, γ-H2Av-positive foci decrease in number and mostly disappear by late region 2b.
source: As meiosis proceeds and the DSBs are repaired, γ-H2Av-positive foci decrease in number and mostly disappear by late region 2b (Jang et al., 2003; Mehrotra and McKim, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: γ-H2Av signals are rarely detected in region three oocytes.
source: γ-H2Av signals are rarely detected in region three oocytes (Figure 3A, arrow).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Wild-type oocytes generate approximately 20–25 Spo11/Mei-W68 dependent breaks during oogenesis.
source: Analysis of mutants that fail to repair DSBs, and thus capture the total number of meiotic breaks, indicate that wild-type oocytes generate approximately 20–25 Spo11/Mei-W68 dependent breaks during oogenesis (Mehrotra and McKim, 2006; Joyce et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In GATOR1 mutants between 50–80% of region three oocytes are γ-H2Av positive.
source: We determined that while the majority of wild-type oocytes had repaired all of their DSBs and thus had no γ-H2Av foci by region 3 of the germarium, in GATOR1 mutants between 50–80% of region three oocytes are γ-H2Av positive (Figure 3A–E,H, arrow) (Mehrotra and McKim, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and quantification shown in Figure 3.

claim: GATOR1 mutant oocytes had a significant increase in the steady state number of γ-H2Av foci per oocyte nucleus in region 2a of the germarium relative to wild-type oocytes.
source: Moreover, GATOR1 mutant oocytes had a significant increase in the steady state number of γ-H2Av foci per oocyte nucleus in region 2a of the germarium relative to wild-type oocytes (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: The GATOR1 complex influences the behavior of meiotic DSB during early oogenesis.
source: From these data, we conclude that the GATOR1 complex influences the behavior of meiotic DSB during early oogenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the γ-H2Av foci data in GATOR1 mutants.

claim: Double-mutant nprl3, mei-P22 oocytes had no γ-H2Av foci.
source: We determined that double-mutant nprl3, mei-P22 oocytes had no γ-H2Av foci (Figure 3F,I and J).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3F,I,J.

claim: The increase in the steady state number of γ-H2Av foci, as well as the retention of these foci into region 3 of the germarium, are dependent on the meiotic DSB machinery.
source: These data indicate that the increase in the steady state number of γ-H2Av foci, as well as the retention of these foci into region 3 of the germarium, are dependent on the meiotic DSB machinery.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the epistasis analysis with mei-P22.

claim: The number of γ-H2Av foci observed in GATOR1 mutant oocytes is never more than the 20–25 foci observed in mutants in the DSB repair pathway.
source: We noticed that the number of γ-H2Av foci observed in GATOR1 mutant oocytes is never more than the 20–25 foci observed in mutants in the DSB repair pathway (Figure 3J) (Mehrotra and McKim, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3J and a citation.

claim: The nprl2, spnA double-mutants contained approximately the same number of γ-H2Av foci as spnA single mutants.
source: However, we found that the nprl2, spnA double-mutants contained approximately the same number of γ-H2Av foci as spnA single mutants (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Mutations in nprl2 do not result in the production of extra meiotic breaks.
source: Thus, mutations in nprl2 do not result in the production of extra meiotic breaks.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the epistasis analysis with spnA.

claim: The GATOR1 complex influences the repair, rather than the production, of meiotic DSBs.
source: Taken together, our data strongly suggest that the GATOR1 complex influences the repair, rather than the production, of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the epistasis analysis showing no increase in DSB number in double mutants.

claim: Approximately 98% of eggs from nprl31 mothers exhibit no DV patterning defects (n = 308).
source: We find that approximately 98% of eggs from nprl31 mothers exhibit no DV patterning defects (n = 308).
evidence: This is based on direct observation and counting of eggs.

claim: 77% of eggs from mutant spnA1 mothers exhibit DV patterning defects (n = 271).
source: In contrast, 77% of eggs from mutant spnA1 mothers exhibit DV patterning defects (n = 271) (Staeva-Vieira et al., 2003).
evidence: This is based on direct observation and counting of eggs, and supported by a citation.

claim: Reducing the dose of S6K lowered the steady state number of meiotic DSBs in iml1 RNAi depletions to levels observed in controls.
source: Notably, reducing the dose of S6K lowered the steady state number of meiotic DSBs in iml1 RNAi depletions to levels observed in controls (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The delay in the repair of meiotic DSBs observed in GATOR1 mutant ovaries is at least in part the result of the hyperactivation of S6K.
source: These data indicate that the delay in the repair of meiotic DSBs observed in GATOR1 mutant ovaries is at least in part the result of the hyperactivation of S6K.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the genetic rescue experiment with S6K.

claim: Late region 2a oocytes in atg1Δ3D germline clones had approximately the same number of γ-H2Av foci as similarly staged wild-type oocytes.
source: We found that late region 2a oocytes in atg1Δ3D germline clones had approximately the same number of γ-H2Av foci as similarly staged wild-type oocytes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The increased number of meiotic DSBs observed in GATOR1 mutants is unlikely to be the result of a block to autophagy.
source: From these data, we conclude that the increased number of meiotic DSBs observed in GATOR1 mutants is unlikely to be the result of a block to autophagy.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the atg1 mutant analysis.

claim: Null mutants of the translational inhibitor 4E-BP/thor do not have an increased steady state number of meiotic DSBs.
source: Similarly, we found that null mutants of the translational inhibitor 4E-BP/thor, which is inhibited by TORC1 activity do not have an increased steady state number of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This is based on experimental observation.

claim: The increase in the steady state number of meiotic DSBs in GATOR1 mutants is not the result of increased translation due to a block to 4E-BP translational inhibition.
source: These data argue that the increase in the steady state number of meiotic DSBs in GATOR1 mutants is not the result of increased translation due to a block to 4E-BP translational inhibition.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the 4E-BP/thor mutant analysis.

claim: During Drosophila oogenesis, the generation of meiotic DSBs results in the brief activation of p53 and the expression of downstream targets.
source: During Drosophila oogenesis, the generation of meiotic DSBs results in the brief activation of p53 and the expression of downstream targets (Figure 5A) (Lu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In wild-type ovaries, a faint signal from the p53-GFPnls reporter is first observed in region 2a of the germarium, concurrent with the generation of meiotic DSBs.
source: In wild-type ovaries, a faint signal from the p53-GFPnls reporter is first observed in region 2a of the germarium, concurrent with the generation of meiotic DSBs (Figure 5A, arrow) (Lu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A and a citation.

claim: By region 3 of the germarium less than 5% of p53-GFPnls ovarian cysts contain detectable levels of GFP.
source: By region 3 of the germarium less than 5% of p53-GFPnls ovarian cysts contain detectable levels of GFP (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The germaria of all three GATOR1 mutants exhibited a dramatic increase in both the strength and the duration of p53-GFPnls expression in the germarium, with strong GFP signal observed in nearly 80% of region three ovarian cysts.
source: In contrast, the germaria of all three GATOR1 mutants exhibited a dramatic increase in both the strength and the duration of p53-GFPnls expression in the germarium, with strong GFP signal observed in nearly 80% of region three ovarian cysts (Figure 5A–D,F,G, arrowheads).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data and quantification shown in Figure 5.

claim: Homozygous germline clones of the iml11 and nprl31 null alleles, hyperactivate p53 confirming that GATOR1 activity is required cell autonomously in the female germline.
source: Homozygous germline clones of the iml11 and nprl31 null alleles, hyperactivate p53 confirming that GATOR1 activity is required cell autonomously in the female germline (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by germline clone data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inhibiting meiotic DSBs strongly suppressed the expression of p53-GFPnls in the nprl3 mutant background.
source: Strikingly, inhibiting meiotic DSBs strongly suppressed the expression of p53-GFPnls in the nprl3 mutant background (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In GATOR1 mutant ovaries, the hyperactivation of p53 is downstream of Spo11/Mei-W68-induced DBS.
source: From these observations, we infer that in GATOR1 mutant ovaries, the hyperactivation of p53 is downstream of Spo11/Mei-W68-induced DBS.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the epistasis analysis with mei-P22.

claim: The GATOR1 complex is required to oppose genotoxic stress triggered by meiotic DSBs and/or other downstream events of meiotic recombination.
source: Moreover, we conclude that the GATOR1 complex is required to oppose genotoxic stress triggered by meiotic DSBs and/or other downstream events of meiotic recombination.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the p53 activation data in GATOR1 mutants.

claim: The p53-GFPnls reporter construct is robustly activated in the germline stem cells and their near descendants in GATOR1 mutant females.
source: As was reported with other mutants that deregulate growth (Wylie et al., 2016), we found that the p53-GFPnls reporter construct is robustly activated in the germline stem cells and their near descendants in GATOR1 mutant females (Figure 5B–D,H).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5 and a citation.

claim: The mei-P22, nprl3 double mutants retain p53-GFPnls expression in stem cells even though the meiotic activation of the p53- GFPnls reporter is lost in regions 2a and 2b of the germarium in the mei-P22, nprl3 double mutant.
source: Consistent with the restriction of Mei-W68/Spo11 activity to meiotic cysts, the mei-P22, nprl3 double mutants retain p53-GFPnls expression in stem cells even though the meiotic activation of the p53- GFPnls reporter is lost in regions 2a and 2b of the germarium in the mei-P22, nprl3 double mutant (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E-G.

claim: An independent cellular stress, likely related to deregulated metabolism or growth, activates p53 in the germline stem cells and cystoblasts of GATOR1 mutant females.
source: Thus, an independent cellular stress, likely related to deregulated metabolism or growth, activates p53 in the germline stem cells and cystoblasts of GATOR1 mutant females.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the differential p53 activation in stem cells versus meiotic cysts.

claim: Depleting Tsc1 in the female germline using RNAi resulted in the robust expression of p53-GFPnls during the early meiotic cycle.
source: We determined that depleting Tsc1 in the female germline using RNAi, resulted in the robust expression of p53-GFPnls during the early meiotic cycle (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A-D.

claim: Tsc1RNAi oocytes had an increase in the steady state number of γ-H2Av foci as well as an increase in the percentage of oocytes that retained γ-H2Av positive into region 3 of the germarium.
source: Moreover, as was observed in GATOR1 mutants, Tsc1RNAi oocytes had an increase in the steady state number of γ-H2Av foci as well as an increase in the percentage of oocytes that retained γ-H2Av positive into region 3 of the germarium (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: The tight control of TORC1 activity by both GATOR1 and TSC is essential to the proper regulation of meiotic DSBs during Drosophila oogenesis.
source: Taken together our data support the model that the tight control of TORC1 activity by both GATOR1 and TSC is essential to the proper regulation of meiotic DSBs during Drosophila oogenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the similar phenotypes of GATOR1 and TSC depletions.

claim: nprl3 mutant larvae were sensitive to DNA damage, with nprl3/Df transheterozygotes exhibiting a greater than 10-fold decrease in survival rates when exposed to 0.08% MMS.
source: Notably, we found that nprl3 mutant larvae were sensitive to DNA damage, with nprl3/Df transheterozygotes exhibiting a greater than 10-fold decrease in survival rates when exposed to 0.08% MMS (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Table 1.

claim: The GATOR1 complex plays a critical role in the response to genotoxic stress in both germline and somatic tissues.
source: These data support the idea that the GATOR1 complex plays a critical role in the response to genotoxic stress in both germline and somatic tissues.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the MMS sensitivity data.

claim: 6 hr after irradiation while wild-type somatic cells have decreased numbers of γ-H2Av positive follicle cells due to rapid DNA repair, nprl3/Df females retain elevated numbers of follicle cells with γ-H2Av foci.
source: However, 6 hr after irradiation while wild-type somatic cells have decreased numbers of γ-H2Av positive follicle cells due to rapid DNA repair, nprl3/Df females retain elevated numbers of follicle cells with γ-H2Av foci. (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In nprl3 mutants the somatic cells of the ovary exhibit a delay in the repair of DSBs.
source: Thus, as is observed in the female germline, in nprl3 mutants the somatic cells of the ovary exhibit a delay in the repair of DSBs.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the γ-H2Av foci persistence data after irradiation.

claim: nprl2 and nprl3 mutant ovaries have increased expression of multiple retrotransposons including TAHRE, Het-A, Indefix and Gypsy.
source: We found that nprl2 and nprl3 mutant ovaries have increased expression of multiple retrotransposons including TAHRE, Het-A, Indefix and Gypsy (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Tsc1RNAi germline resulted in little or no increase in retrotransposon expression.
source: In contrast to nprl2 and nprl3 mutants, Tsc1RNAi germline resulted in little or no increase in retrotransposon expression (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The GATOR1 components nprl2 and nprl3 oppose retrotransposon expression in the female germline of Drosophila.
source: From these results, we conclude that the GATOR1 components nprl2 and nprl3 oppose retrotransposon expression in the female germline of Drosophila.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the qRT-PCR data showing increased retrotransposon expression in GATOR1 mutants.

claim: spnA/Rad51 mutant ovaries had increased levels of retrotransposon expression.
source: Intriguingly, we found that spnA/Rad51 mutant ovaries had increased levels of retrotransposon expression (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The increased levels of retrotransposon expression observed in GATOR1 mutant ovaries may be due, at least in part, to the delay in the repair of meiotic DSBs.
source: Thus, our data are consistent with the model that the increased levels of retrotransposon expression observed in GATOR1 mutant ovaries may be due, at least in part, to the delay in the repair of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between DSB repair defects and retrotransposon expression.

claim: Retrotransposon expression was largely, but not completely, suppressed in nprl3, mei-P22 double-mutant ovaries.
source: Using qRT-PCR we observed that retrotransposon expression was largely, but not completely, suppressed in nprl3, mei-P22 double-mutant ovaries.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Meiotic DSBs trigger the expression of retrotransposons during Drosophila oogenesis in the nprl3 mutant background.
source: Thus, meiotic DSBs trigger the expression of retrotransposons during Drosophila oogenesis in the nprl3 mutant background (Figure 8B).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the partial suppression of retrotransposon expression when DSBs are blocked.

claim: The GATOR1 complex may also impact retrotransposon expression independent of meiotic DSBs.
source: However, it is important to note that these data suggest that the GATOR1 complex may also impact retrotransposon expression independent of meiotic DSBs as indicated by the relatively modest rescue of TAHRE over-expression observed in nprl3, mei-P22 double mutants (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is inferred from the incomplete rescue of retrotransposon expression in double mutants.

claim: The p53, nprl3 double mutant ovaries showed a dramatic increase in retrotransposon expression relative to either single mutant.
source: Strikingly, the p53, nprl3 double mutant ovaries showed a dramatic increase in retrotransposon expression relative to either single mutant (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The p53 and nprl3 phenotypes are additive with respect to the inhibition of retrotransposon expression.
source: Thus, the p53 and nprl3 phenotypes are additive with respect to the inhibition of retrotransposon expression.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the epistasis analysis showing additive effects.

claim: GATOR1 and p53 act through independent pathways to inhibit retrotransposon activation in the female germline during meiosis.
source: These data strongly suggest that GATOR1 and p53 act through independent pathways to inhibit retrotransposon activation in the female germline during meiosis (Figure 8C).
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the additive phenotype in double mutants.

claim: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the down-regulation of TORC1 by SEACIT/GATOR1 in response to amino acid stress promotes both meiotic entry and early meiotic progression.
source: In the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the down-regulation of TORC1 by SEACIT/GATOR1 in response to amino acid stress promotes both meiotic entry and early meiotic progression (Deutschbauer et al., 2002; Jordan et al., 2007; Neklesa and Davis, 2009; Spielewoy et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: During Drosophila oogenesis the GATOR1 complex promotes meiotic entry.
source: Surprisingly, as is observed in yeast, during Drosophila oogenesis the GATOR1 complex promotes meiotic entry (Wei et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Restraining TORC1 activity via a pathway that involves both GATOR1 and the Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) promotes the timely repair of meiotic DSBs and prevents the hyperactivation of p53 in the female germline.
source: We find that restraining TORC1 activity via a pathway that involves both GATOR1 and the Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) promotes the timely repair of meiotic DSBs and prevents the hyperactivation of p53 in the female germline.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from GATOR1 and TSC mutant analyses.

claim: The delayed repair of meiotic DSBs in GATOR1 mutants is due, at least in part, to the hyperactivation of the TORC1 target S6K.
source: Notably, the delayed repair of meiotic DSBs in GATOR1 mutants is due, at least in part, to the hyperactivation of the TORC1 target S6K.
evidence: This is supported by genetic rescue experiments with S6K.

claim: The GATOR2 component Mio opposes the activity of GATOR1 in the female germline, thus preventing the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity and allowing for the growth and development of the oocyte in later stages of oogenesis.
source: Conversely, our data indicate that the GATOR2 component Mio opposes the activity of GATOR1 in the female germline, thus preventing the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity and allowing for the growth and development of the oocyte in later stages of oogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing rescue of mio phenotypes by blocking DSBs.

claim: A regulatory loop is required to modulate TORC1 activity in response to meiotic DSBs during Drosophila oogenesis.
source: Thus, we have identified a regulatory loop required to modulate TORC1 activity in response to meiotic DSBs during Drosophila oogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on GATOR1, GATOR2, and meiotic DSBs.

claim: The GATOR1 complex prevents the derepression of retrotransposon expression in the presence of meiotic DSBs.
source: Finally, during the course of our studies, we observed that the GATOR1 complex prevents the derepression of retrotransposon expression in the presence of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data showing increased retrotransposon expression in GATOR1 mutants.

claim: In yeast and Drosophila SEACIT/GATOR1 mutants share a common meiotic phenotype, the delayed repair of meiotic DSBs.
source: Thus, yeast and Drosophila SEACIT/GATOR1 mutants share a common meiotic phenotype, the delayed repair of meiotic DSBs.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the phenotypes in yeast and Drosophila.

claim: Low TORC1 activity may be a common feature of the early meiotic cycle in many organisms.
source: These results raise the intriguing possibility that low TORC1 activity may be a common feature of the early meiotic cycle in many organisms.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the conservation of the phenotype.

claim: In mammals, S6K has been implicated in the regulation of the DNA damage response with hyperactivation of the TORC1-S6K pathway resulting in the accumulation of unrepaired DSBs and genome instability.
source: Intriguingly, in mammals, S6K has been implicated in the regulation of the DNA damage response with hyperactivation of the TORC1-S6K pathway resulting in the accumulation of unrepaired DSBs and genome instability (Lai et al., 2010; Xie et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Similar to what is reported in mammals, the hyperactivity of the TORC1/S6K axis delays the repair of DSBs in Drosophila.
source: Thus, similar to what is reported in mammals, our data are consistent with the model that the hyperactivity of the TORC1/S6K axis delays the repair of DSBs in Drosophila.
evidence: This is inferred from the S6K rescue experiments and comparison to mammalian data.

claim: GATOR1 mutant embryos have a reduced ability to survive low levels of γ-irradiation.
source: Similar to what is observed in TSC mutant cells in humans that have increased levels of TORC1 activity, we find that GATOR1 mutant embryos have a reduced ability to survive low levels of γ-irradiation (Paterson et al., 1982; Deschavanne and Fertil, 1996; Lee et al., 2007; Pai et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by MMS sensitivity data and citations to prior literature.

claim: In the somatic follicle cells of the ovary a delay in the repair of DSBs was observed after adult females are exposed to low levels of γ-irradiation.
source: Moreover, in the somatic follicle cells of the ovary we observed a delay in the repair of DSBs after adult females are exposed to low levels of γ-irradiation.
evidence: This is supported by γ-H2Av foci data after irradiation.

claim: In Drosophila inappropriately high TORC1 activity delays the repair of DSBs in both the germline and somatic tissues.
source: Thus, in Drosophila inappropriately high TORC1 activity delays the repair of DSBs in both the germline and somatic tissues.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the combined data on germline and somatic DSB repair.

claim: Germ line cells may be at an increased risk for transposon derepression due to the genotoxic stress associated with meiotic recombination.
source: Thus, germ line cells may be at an increased risk for transposon derepression due to the genotoxic stress associated with meiotic recombination.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the presence of DSBs during meiosis.

claim: In GATOR1 mutants, the DSBs that initiate meiotic recombination trigger the deregulation of retrotransposon expression.
source: In line with these studies, we find that in GATOR1 mutants, the DSBs that initiate meiotic recombination trigger the deregulation of retrotransposon expression.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data showing increased retrotransposon expression in GATOR1 mutants that is partially suppressed by blocking DSBs.

claim: p53 mutant females derepress retrotransposon expression during oogenesis, but primarily in the presence of meiotic DSBs.
source: Similarly, p53 mutant females derepress retrotransposon expression during oogenesis, but as observed in GATOR1 mutants, primarily in the presence of meiotic DSBs (Wylie et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The GATOR1 complex may influence retrotransposon expression independent of the regulation of TORC1 activity.
source: However, our data also suggest that the GATOR1 complex may influence retrotransposon expression independent of the regulation of TORC1 activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of GATOR1 and TSC depletions on retrotransposon expression.

claim: The depletion of GATOR1 components, but not TSC components result in the activation of LINE1 expression in HeLa cells.
source: As is observed with spnA the depletion of GATOR1 components, but not TSC components result in the activation of LINE1 expression in HeLa cells (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The GATOR1 complex may impact retrotransposon expression in the germline via two independent pathways: First by promoting the repair of meiotic DSBs through the downregulation of TORC1 activity and second via a pathway that functions independent of TORC1 inhibition.
source: Taken together, these data hint that the GATOR1 complex may impact retrotransposon expression in the germline via two independent pathways: First by promoting the repair of meiotic DSBs through the downregulation of TORC1 activity and second via a pathway that functions independent of TORC1 inhibition.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the combined data from GATOR1, TSC, and retrotransposon expression.

claim: Genes encoding components of the GATOR1 complex are often deleted in cancers.
source: Genes encoding components of the GATOR1 complex are often deleted in cancers (Lerman and Minna, 2000; Ji et al., 2002; Ueda et al., 2006; Bar-Peled et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Cancer cells frequently have increased TORC1 activity, increased genomic instability and increased retrotransposon expression.
source: As is observed in GATOR1 mutants, cancer cells frequently have increased TORC1 activity, increased genomic instability and increased retrotransposon expression.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cancer cells.

claim: Meiotic DSBs activate, or are required to maintain, a GATOR1/TSC dependent pathway that downregulates TORC1 activity in the female germline.
source: Meiotic DSBs activate, or are required to maintain, a GATOR1/TSC dependent pathway that downregulates TORC1 activity in the female germline (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data, illustrated in Figure 9A.

claim: The GATOR2 component Mio is required to oppose or turnoff the GATOR1/TSC pathway to prevent the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity in later stages of oogenesis.
source: The GATOR2 component Mio is required to oppose or turnoff this pathway to prevent the constitutive downregulation of TORC1 activity in later stages of oogenesis.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data showing rescue of mio phenotypes.

claim: In npr3 mutants in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, npr3 mutant cells enter meiosis and express the transcription factor and master regulator of gametogenesis IME1 with wild-type kinetics.
source: In the sporulation proficient strain SK1, npr3 mutant cells enter meiosis and express the transcription factor and master regulator of gametogenesis IME1 with wild-type kinetics (Jordan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In yeast npr3 mutants exhibit a mild delay in the generation of meiotic DNA breaks, but a substantial delay in the repair of meiotic DSBs.
source: Subsequently, npr3 mutants exhibit a mild delay in the generation of meiotic DNA breaks, but a substantial delay in the repair of meiotic DSBs (Jordan et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.
